Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.dc: Manny Rojas, at Delaware since 2020 — predating Ryan Carty, who kept him.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide uses two seasons as a controlled comparison to show the size of the FBS jump: 21 points and 5.3 yards per play allowed in Delaware's final FCS season, against 31 points and 6.0 in the first FBS season, with the run defense at 4.6 yards per carry overall.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide breaks down a poor 3.8 yards per carry to show the line is not solely responsible — Nick Minicucci had 112 carries for just 235 yards, an average of 2.1 that dragged the whole figure down.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Minicucci throwing for nearly 3,700 yards with a 23-to-7 ratio and flags a specific durability concern: he takes a lot of hits and the depth behind him is virtually non-existent.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.continuity: Complete. The Stability Score table (p. 42) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 2 for 12 returning starters — totalling 16.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.staff_turnover: None recorded, and the guide notes the defensive coordinator predates the head coach and was retained — while raising the question of how long that loyalty survives another poor year.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.portal_recruiting: Addressed by omission on the offensive line: since this was not an area Delaware filled through the portal, the guide concludes the programme must hope internal options improve. It records a few FBS-level transfers added on defense.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.vsin_assessment: Institutional achievement credited, with a sober look at the underlying numbers. The guide's framing is that accomplishments matter to recent FCS-to-FBS arrivals, so the 68 Ventures Bowl upset of Louisiana was a huge one for the trophy case. It reads the arrow as pointing up in year two with more scholarships and more depth, and its balanced verdict is that Carty appears to be a solid coach and this appears to be a good programme, but Delaware was out-gained per play and struggled in the trenches within a subpar conference. It lists the margins that defined league play — three-point losses to Western Kentucky and Sam Houston State, a three-point win over Middle Tennessee and a one-point win over Louisiana Tech — and expects coin flips to decide the season again, closing on how Carty and his staff adjust now that everyone has film on the Blue Hens.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.strengths: A Stability Score of 16 with everything returning, a bowl win in the first FBS season, a quarterback with nearly 3,700 yards and a 23-to-7 ratio, all the running backs and the top receiver back, three of the four leading tacklers returning, and more scholarships and depth in year two.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.concerns: A defense that jumped from 21 to 31 points allowed on the move up with a run defense at 4.6 yards per carry, two long-term offensive line starters gone with no portal replacement, virtually non-existent quarterback depth behind a starter who takes a lot of hits, and being out-gained per play in conference play.
Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its projection is 5.73 wins.

FIU Golden Panthers.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide records Willie Simmons as previously head coach at Florida A&M and Prairie View A&M, and calls him college football's Mike Tomlin for never having had a losing season as a head coach.
FIU Golden Panthers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
FIU Golden Panthers.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
FIU Golden Panthers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
FIU Golden Panthers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
FIU Golden Panthers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's key numbers are the conference-only splits — better than 6.2 yards per play gained and just over 5.6 allowed — and it states the methodological principle behind using them: for teams like this it is always important to parse out the paycheck games, since trips to Penn State and UConn carry little merit in the metrics or as a guide to the next season.
FIU Golden Panthers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
FIU Golden Panthers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records coordinator Nick Coleman and Simmons landing JJ Kohl, originally at Iowa State and then Appalachian State, where he posted a 12-to-2 ratio, and notes he was a four-star in the 2023 class and is a massive human being at 6-foot-7 and 245 pounds — while adding it would not be terribly surprised to see him share time with Delaware transfer Zach Marker or freshman DJ Alexander, both bigger running threats.
FIU Golden Panthers.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 7 returning starters, totalling 10.
FIU Golden Panthers.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
FIU Golden Panthers.prior_school: Florida A&M and Prairie View A&M for Simmons. On the roster the guide records JJ Kohl from Iowa State by way of Appalachian State, Zach Marker from Delaware, projected starting corners from Duke and FAU, a multi-time transfer most recently from Oklahoma State, and two-year South Alabama starter Wesley Miller.
FIU Golden Panthers.portal_recruiting: The rebuilding mechanism, and the guide describes the secondary as a grab bag of transfers.
FIU Golden Panthers.vsin_assessment: An unsung hero of the coaching ranks, with a structural caution attached. The guide names Simmons an unsung hero of the 2025 coaching ranks for taking FIU bowling for the first time since 2019, gives the preceding context of Mike MacIntyre's three 4-8 seasons, and records that Simmons delivered FIU's first winning conference record since 2018 and nearly as many conference wins in one year, five, as MacIntyre managed in three, six. Its structural caution is that despite the financial commitment from Armando Christian Perez — better known as Pitbull — and the school's Florida location, this has been a hard place to win and a hard place to sustain winning. It is explicit that this is not a criticism of the team: what Simmons is doing is very impressive, and FIU will be highly competitive again.
FIU Golden Panthers.strengths: A head coach who has never had a losing season, full coordinator continuity, conference-only splits that gained more than 6.2 yards per play and allowed just over 5.6, a large and productive portal quarterback addition, financial backing from a high-profile donor, and good safety play.
FIU Golden Panthers.concerns: The leading quarterback, running back, receiver, tackler and defensive back all gone; only seven returning starters; a secondary rebuilt as a grab bag of transfers; and a turnover dependence the guide flags — FIU's quarterbacks threw 13 interceptions while the defense produced 21 takeaways, leaving the team exactly even in margin.
FIU Golden Panthers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching, though the guide judges FIU plenty capable of seven or eight wins if the ball bounces its way.

Jacksonville State Gamecocks.previous_hc_experience: None before this. The guide records Charles Kelly as an assistant at Jacksonville State back in the mid-1990s, now in his first head-coaching job with a successful year one behind him, and calls the hire savvy.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.oc: Taylor Housewright, promoted from tight ends coach, bringing experience from two years as coordinator at Montana State. Clint Trickett left for the same role at Maryland.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.oc_status: New — the guide records Trickett's departure and Housewright's promotion, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's expectation is a little more throwing from Caden Creel while the staff waits for a back to step forward, and that 6-foot-8 receiver Deondre Johnson becomes more of a focal point.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.run_pass: The programme's identity, and the guide states it as such — an established programme that, even through mild downturns, can run the ball. It records the bell-cow workload being replaced: Cam Cook's 295 carries and 16 rushing touchdowns.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide's stated reason for hope is efficiency: the offense was much better with Creel at the helm than with Rutgers and Kentucky transfer Gavin Wimsatt, and Creel is himself a 1,000-yard rusher who also threw for over 1,500 yards.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.continuity: Head coach, defensive coordinator and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes but is promoted from within. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 0, 3 and 4, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 12.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator, handled by internal promotion.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.prior_school: Jacksonville State itself for Kelly, who was an assistant there in the mid-1990s. Maryland is where Clint Trickett went, and Montana State is Housewright's coordinator background. The guide also notes Rich Rodriguez is back at West Virginia where it all started.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.portal_recruiting: Addressed as a collection of small-school transfers and homegrown players getting more opportunity at receiver.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.vsin_assessment: Credit to the programme rather than one coach, with an explicit regression warning. The guide credits the run continuing under both Rich Rodriguez and Charles Kelly and calls the Kelly hire savvy. It then argues the nine-win streak concealed decline: Jacksonville State scored nearly eight fewer points per game year over year while benefitting greatly from a +10 turnover margin and a lot of close wins, itemising a 7-2 conference record with wins by 10, 2, 13, 3, 3, 9 and 3. It restates the structural point that the Gamecocks are +24 in turnover margin since joining the conference, and its balanced conclusion is that Jacksonville State did average over six yards per play in conference games and did out-gain opponents, but not by enough to justify a 7-2 record.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.strengths: A programme the guide says has sustained success across two head coaches, defensive-coordinator and quarterback continuity, a quarterback the guide says might be the best in the conference, an internal coordinator promotion with prior coordinator experience, and a distinctive 6-foot-8 receiving target.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.concerns: The loss of a 1,659-yard bell-cow back with no clear replacement, a receiving corps reduced to one significant returnee, a red-zone touchdown percentage ranked 93rd on 59 trips, and a record the guide says was inflated by a +10 turnover margin and a run of close wins.
Jacksonville State Gamecocks.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its projection is 7.47 wins.

Kennesaw State Owls.oc: Mitch Militello, from the Josh Heupel coaching tree.
Kennesaw State Owls.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Kennesaw State Owls.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Kennesaw State Owls.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Kennesaw State Owls.offensive_scheme: Not named, but its lineage and likely direction are: coordinator Mitch Militello comes from the Josh Heupel tree, and the guide wonders whether he now has the personnel to play faster.
Kennesaw State Owls.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide grades the unit against a low bar and still finds it wanting — this is not a good offensive conference, yet the Owls allowed more than 400 yards per game and were out-gained by 0.5 yards per carry — and isolates a schedule-strength effect at nearly 6.5 yards per play allowed in November.
Kennesaw State Owls.tempo: Expected to rise. Kennesaw State averaged 69 plays per game last season, and the guide would not be surprised to see that increase.
Kennesaw State Owls.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Kennesaw State Owls.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide credits Jerry Mack with hitting a home run on Amari Odom, who stabilised the offense and supplied a dual-threat component, and records the replacements as Rickie Collins from Syracuse and JUCO starter Landon Varnes, who threw 31 touchdowns against 14 interceptions at Mississippi Gulf Coast and chose the Owls over Arkansas State and Eastern Michigan.
Kennesaw State Owls.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 11.
Kennesaw State Owls.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Kennesaw State Owls.prior_school: Syracuse, in both directions — Amari Odom left for it and Rickie Collins arrived from it. Mississippi Gulf Coast is Landon Varnes' background.
Kennesaw State Owls.portal_recruiting: The programme's method, and the guide quantifies it: Mack brought in more than 60 players via the portal last year, and 247Sports lists 29 graded transfers this cycle in a class ranked third in the conference behind Sam Houston and Liberty.
Kennesaw State Owls.vsin_assessment: An extraordinary turnaround, with the repeatability question asked plainly. The guide records 2-10 as a first-year FBS member in 2024 becoming 10-4 and a conference title with a first-year head coach and a lot of new personnel, calls the eight-win improvement incredible — especially with Power Four openers against Wake Forest and Indiana — and credits Mack with rebuilding the roster quickly. It then sets out both sides: it is fair to be excited that transfers who did not feature prominently now get their chance in year two of the system, but there is basically zero returning production on offense, and it asks what the chances are of lightning striking twice. Its summary defensive statistic is that Kennesaw State was out-gained in four of its eight conference wins.
Kennesaw State Owls.strengths: A head coach who produced an eight-win improvement and a conference title in year one, full coordinator continuity, a coordinator from the Josh Heupel tree with the personnel possibly now in place to play faster, the top three tacklers returning, and the third-ranked portal class in the conference.
Kennesaw State Owls.concerns: Basically zero returning production on offense with all the running backs and all but two receivers gone, an unresolved quarterback competition, a defense that allowed more than 400 yards per game in a weak offensive conference and was out-gained in four of eight conference wins, and a November stretch at nearly 6.5 yards per play allowed.
Kennesaw State Owls.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching.

Liberty Flames.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide measures the 4-8 season against Jamey Chadwell's own career, calling it his worst record since 2017, when he was interim head coach at Coastal Carolina while Joe Moglia dealt with health issues and the Chanticleers went 3-9.
Liberty Flames.oc: Not addressed by name; the guide attributes the offensive system to Chadwell.
Liberty Flames.dc: Shawn Quinn, Virginia Tech's outside linebackers coach, who went 16-6 as head coach at Savannah State before joining the Hokies.
Liberty Flames.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Liberty Flames.dc_status: The guide states this two ways — see the conflicts field. The team pages (pp. 196–197) record Chadwell beginning year four alongside a new defensive coordinator and devote a section to whether Shawn Quinn is the right man for the job, while the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Liberty Flames.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Liberty Flames.offensive_scheme: Named by mechanism. The guide explains that Chadwell's offense is predicated on heavy pre-snap motion to get players into space, and explains why last season failed it: Ethan Vasko did not make those throws. It also records a change of identity — pass-first when he had Grayson McCall, now run-first, with 508 carries against 316 pass attempts last season.
Liberty Flames.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide identifies the failing to be fixed precisely: Liberty allowed 0.7 more yards per carry than in the two previous seasons, which it calls exactly what a linebackers coach turned coordinator should be able to fix.
Liberty Flames.run_pass: Stated and changed — run-first now, at 508 carries against 316 pass attempts, with the guide concluding the quarterbacks only need to complete enough passes to keep defenses honest.
Liberty Flames.qb_development: Framed as a dependency the guide treats sceptically. It says it is hardly a coincidence Chadwell was preparing to leave Coastal Carolina just as Grayson McCall ran out of eligibility, records that bringing former Chanticleer Ethan Vasko with him did not work out — a 10-to-12 ratio, under 2,000 passing yards and 2.6 yards per carry — and notes portal addition Deshawn Purdie is only a 50% passer across 282 attempts. Its verdict is that Chadwell has options, but whether any is good remains to be seen.
Liberty Flames.continuity: Head coach returns and the defensive coordinator column prints returning points; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 9. The team pages describe the defensive coordinator position differently — see the conflicts field.
Liberty Flames.staff_turnover: The team pages record a new defensive coordinator in Shawn Quinn and treat the hire as the season's biggest selling point.
Liberty Flames.prior_school: Coastal Carolina, which recurs — Chadwell's previous programme, Ethan Vasko's origin, and where the guide notes Quinn was defensive coordinator at Charleston Southern the year before Chadwell took over there, so the two have probably crossed paths without ever working together. Virginia Tech and Savannah State are Quinn's background. On the roster the guide records Deshawn Purdie from Wake Forest, Kanye Udoh from Army by way of Arizona State, Peyton Jones from Duke and Kam Davis from Florida State.
Liberty Flames.portal_recruiting: Rated highly at one position. The guide names former Army running back Kanye Udoh one of the top free-agent pickups in the conference, and records receiver transfers from Charleston Southern and Indiana.
Liberty Flames.vsin_assessment: A bad season attributed to details, with the coordinator hire as the stated reason for optimism. The guide's own reading of 2025 is a team that did not pay attention to the details — more interceptions than passing touchdowns, no sacks or takeaways on defense, and not much apparent leadership. It expects a bounce-back in year four with a new defensive coordinator, and calls the Quinn hire its biggest selling point: Virginia Tech almost always has a strong defense, and it rates him as someone who can identify talent in the DMV at a very high level. It also argues coordinator hires matter at any programme but especially in the Group of Six, because talent levels vary so much.
Liberty Flames.strengths: A head coach with a strong career record and a defined offensive system, a coordinator hire the guide calls its biggest selling point with head-coaching experience and DMV recruiting reach, one of the conference's top portal pickups at running back, greater depth at quarterback and running back, and an offensive line the guide says looks significantly better.
Liberty Flames.concerns: A 4-8 season the guide attributes to a lack of attention to detail, a quarterback room where neither option has passed well, a run-first identity that depends on defenses being kept honest, and a defense that allowed 0.7 more yards per carry than in the two previous seasons.
Liberty Flames.betting: Projection is 8.24 wins, with a stated liking for Liberty's chances to win more of the close games. The coaching-linked basis is the Quinn hire and the expectation of a better run defense, which the guide says should make a huge difference.
Liberty Flames.conflicts: The guide states the defensive coordinator position two ways. The team pages (pp. 196–197) record Jamey Chadwell beginning year four alongside a new defensive coordinator and devote a full section to Shawn Quinn's arrival from Virginia Tech, while the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator. Both are reproduced as printed and neither is corrected.
